text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High p99 latency on shared-gpu-pool-3 — p99 generation latency >= 2.5s for last 5m (streaming stalls observed). Auto-page to #incidents and oncall.

sara: I'm on it, taking pager. seeing p95 ~350ms but p99 jumped to ~2.7s on metrics dashboard. streaming stall count up ~180 in 5m.

leo: any customer-facing alerts yet? jamie?

jamie: no customer emails yet, but two support tickets flagged slow responses for chat embeddings. marking as potential impact.

reza: quick signal from runtime: IO wait on hosts nvme0 spiking; cgroup writeback rising on containers in tenant-id T-934. suspect noisy tenant causing multi-tenant IO contention.

mika: confirmed KV-cache misses increased concurrently. prefix cache eviction rate shot up. could be long-context synthetic requests.

ada: can we get top p99 pods by host / tenant? run `kubectl top pods --all-namespaces` won't show IO but we have a script: `scripts/host-top-io.sh`

leo: run that and paste results.

reza: running now...
```
HOST: gpu-host-27 nvme0_io_wait=42% tenant=T-934 pods=[t934-worker-1,t934-worker-2]
HOST: gpu-host-26 nvme0_io_wait=40% tenant=T-101 pods=[t101-worker-3]
HOST: gpu-host-25 nvme0_io_wait=5% tenant=shared pools normal
```

reza: T-934 looks dominant. their streaming sessions show many concurrent long-run decoders (~30 per host).

sara: want to live-mitigate: options — throttle T-934, cgroup iops cap, or evacuate to isolated pool. Evac safer but takes ~3-5m to spin up nodes. Throttle quicker.

mika: suggestion: apply temporary cgroup blkio limits on the three top hosts for T-934 containers to reduce write bandwidth, and enable ioqos on the host for tenant fairness. Also bump kv-cache size for other tenants to reduce misses.

ada: I'm prepping a canary config to cap T-934 at 60% of previous IO. command ready: `tc qdisc replace dev eth0 root fq_codel limit 1000` (but that's network; real command below)

reza: actual blkio command:
```
echo 1048576 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/containers/<container-id>/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device
```
I'll iteratively cap on gpu-host-27/26 for containers matching T-934.

leo: do it but staggered. we want to avoid mass drop causing client errors. Execute on host-27 first. call out before change.

sara: on gpu-host-27 now. applying cap to t934-worker-1 and t934-worker-2.

ops-bot: action: blkio cap applied to containers [t934-worker-1,t934-worker-2] on gpu-host-27 by sara at 2026-03-15T14:12:05Z :white_check_mark:

leo: metrics?

mika: p99 dropped from 2.7s -> 1.4s within 40s, streaming stalls halved. good signal.

reza: nvme0_io_wait on gpu-host-27 down from 42% -> 18%. gpu-host-26 still elevated.

sara: applying cap on gpu-host-26 (t934-worker-3) now.

ops-bot: action: blkio cap applied to containers [t934-worker-3] on gpu-host-26 by sara at 2026-03-15T14:15:12Z :white_check_mark:

leo: p99 now 980ms, p95 stable ~320ms. streaming stalls trending down. nice.

jamie: noted in support: T-934 chat threads showing timeouts for a subset of requests — potential partial degradation. Will notify customers in impacted bucket with status update.

ada: we should spin up isolation pool for T-934 to avoid repeated events. provisioning nodes now with reserved IO profile (isolated-pool-5). ETA ~4m.

reza: also adding a QOS rule: tenant-based IO weight so no single tenant can saturate host NVMe. Will push policy when isolation is ready.

mika: while that's provisioning, can we roll back blkio caps gradually after isolation completes. plan: migrate T-934 pods onto isolated pool, verify metrics for 5m, then remove throttles.

sara: agreed. start migration once nodes ready. assignees: reza (migration), ada (deploy hooks), mika (observability).

ops-bot: event: nodes isolated-pool-5:3 ready at 2026-03-15T14:18:40Z

reza: starting `kubectl drain` and `kubectl delete pod` to force evict T-934 pods onto isolated pool via node-affinity. doing in small batches of 3.

```
for pod in $(kubectl get pods -l tenant=T-934 -o name | head -n3); do kubectl delete $pod; sleep 15; done
```

reza: migrating batch 1 -> success.

mika: host io metrics for gpu-host-27/26 returning to baseline. p99 now 420ms. streaming stall count ~10 in last 5m.

leo: any error spikes or 5xx from hosts?

jamie: support reported ~12 timed-out requests during mitigation window but retries succeeded. Customer impact limited to increased latency and some client retries. I'll post an advisory to affected customers: short-lived latency spikes and partial throttling applied; mitigation in progress.

sara: ok we're in remediation; creating incident doc and starting postmortem template. tagging severity S3 for now due to partial customer impact but broad SLO touch.

ada: after final batch migrated, I'll remove blkio caps and apply permanent tenant IO weight policy.

ops-bot: migration complete for tenant T-934 at 2026-03-15T14:22:55Z :white_check_mark:

reza: removing blkio caps now.

ops-bot: blkio caps removed on gpu-host-27/26 by reza at 2026-03-15T14:23:40Z :white_check_mark:

mika: p99 stable ~310ms, streaming stalls back to normal. KV-cache eviction rate normalized.

leo: great. action items: 1) add tenant IO weight policy (reza) 2) update autoscaler to detect long-run decoders and autospawn isolated pool (ada) 3) postmortem draft and customer notes (jamie + sara).

sara: handing off to oncall-2 (leo) for monitoring the next 2 hours. leaving notes in incident doc.

leo: taking handoff. I'll monitor p99/p95 and the migration logs. If any regression, I will re-open pager.

incident-bot: INC-2026-0315-007 created, severity=S3, owner=sara, linked tickets=[SUP-7829].

jamie: posting customer advisory now.

leo: thanks team. low-level followups in postmortem. :thumbsup:
